about: The decks that have a per-deck bot or a candidate for one, and where each one's measurements are. runner/bots.py turns this into demo-data/bots.json for the dashboard. Edited by hand when a playbook ships or a run comes in. `tables` is the deck's latest paired exam among bots (since 2026-11-12 the round on the pool of twelve); `pool_of_four_tables` is the exam it joined the pool on and `stock_tables` the old exam at three stock seats, both kept for the record.

bots.status: shipped (v5, 2026-11-22: version 4 with a guard on its attack: attackers are taken back when the attack would leave the seat where the opponents, one after another, are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that). Versions 3, 4 and 5 were played on the same 200 tables at the owner's table, every other seat a version of 2026-11-21 with its hooks (ab-run #57, tables that chose nothing): wins 56, 72 and 71. Version 4 beside version 3: 33 tables against 17, exact test 0.03; version 5 beside version 4: 2 against 3, exact test 1.00, the seat dead with its own creatures tapped 19 times where it was 21. Both stand by rules fixed before the run and read over the ten decks together (the hooks: 186 tables against 155; the guard: 38 against 41, with 169 such deaths against 193). The comparison with the stock pilot is version 2's: at the owner's table, on tables that chose nothing, +1.5 points on its stock pilot (75 tables against 72, 95% -7 to +10, exact test 0.83), ahead, not clear of noise. The exam version 2 shipped on, at tables of the pool of twelve: +12.5 points on its stock pilot (91 tables against 66, 95% +4 to +21, exact test 0.0046), clear of noise. The attack is the better of two on these tables: the same rules won 86 with the go-wide attack
bots.summary: Clavileño at once, anthems and engines in order, March of the Canonized with X; Olivia's Wrath once it has three Vampires (it spares them), Austere Command and Damn through Forge's own judgement when it is behind, Patron of the Vein on a target. Version 3 also casts New Blood, which neither pilot ever cast: it takes the best creature worth four or more of the opponent that looks most dangerous. Version 4 casts Pact of the Serpent on itself, which no pilot ever cast (a card for each Vampire, with three or more of them, twenty life and fewer Vampires than life); and it no longer leaves everything about the other players to Forge: it takes the sure kill of the most dangerous opponent, aims its attack at that opponent when the attack is no worse there, attacks an opponent who cannot block with creatures that would have stayed home and aims its removal triggers at the most dangerous opponent. Version 5 also keeps attackers home when the attack would leave it dead before its next turn.
